A LITTLE DIRECTION

The way around.

01

Start where you are.

Use your location, search for a place, enter latitude and longitude, or choose a point on the map.

02

Ride your kind of ride.

Pick your terrain and distance. CIRKVL searches in different directions, routes along mapped roads and trails, then ranks up to five distinct loops by terrain match and distance.

03

Take the loop with you.

Save it here or export GPX. In the Suunto app, open Maps → + → Import route (.gpx), save the route, and enable it for your watch. GPX also works with other apps that support route imports.

Suunto’s import guide ↗
What the terrain numbers mean

Surface percentages are weighted by section distance using OpenStreetMap surface tags returned by BRouter. Missing or broad tags such as “unpaved” stay unknown. Gravel includes gravel, fine gravel, and compacted surfaces. Trail share is an estimate from path and MTB tags; a narrow single track cannot be guaranteed where widths are unmapped. Your preferred terrain is a preference, and connecting sections can use other surfaces.

Roads, trail access, and conditions can change. Review the map and respect signs and local access rules. Sparse networks, coasts, and service availability may produce fewer than five loops. Actual length and any repeated sections are shown.

Open data & your location

Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Routing and elevation by BRouter. Map rendering by Leaflet. CIRKVL has no account, tracking scripts, or analytics.

Your location is requested only when you tap the location button. Route waypoints go to the routing service when you generate a ride, search text goes to Nominatim when you search, and the map service receives the viewed tile area. Saved routes remain in this browser’s local storage and won’t sync to other devices. Online services are needed for new routes and maps.
